		<link>https://cryptoslate.com/the-uk-police-raids-on-people-trading-crypto-for-cash-raises-a-hard-question-about-financial-freedom/</link>

					<description><![CDATA[<p>UK authorities have carried out their first coordinated operation against suspected illegal peer-to-peer crypto trading, sending a clear and simple message to the market: once a person turns crypto dealing into a business, the state expects names, checks, records, and accountability. The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) said it worked with police and tax officials to […]</p>
<p>The post <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/the-uk-police-raids-on-people-trading-crypto-for-cash-raises-a-hard-question-about-financial-freedom/">UK police raids on people trading crypto for cash raises a hard question about financial freedom</a> appeared first on <a href="https://cryptoslate.com">CryptoSlate</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>UK authorities have carried out their first coordinated operation against suspected <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/uks-fca-takes-action-against-illegal-crypto-atm-operators/">illegal</a> peer-to-peer crypto trading, sending a clear and simple message to the market: once a person turns crypto dealing into a business, the state expects names, checks, records, and accountability.</p>
<p>The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) <a href="https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/uk-targets-illegal-crypto-trading-london-crackdown-2026-04-22/">said</a> it worked with police and tax officials to visit eight London addresses linked to suspected illegal p2p crypto trading, issuing cease-and-desist letters at each site. Evidence gathered during the inspections is now supporting criminal investigations, according to the regulator, while <em>Reuters</em> reported that there are currently no FCA-registered peer-to-peer crypto traders in Britain.</p>
<p>The legal side is fairly easy to understand. In the UK, an occasional person-to-person crypto trade isn’t the same as running a dealing desk, brokerage service, or informal exchange. The line is crossed when someone regularly exchanges crypto for money, arranges those exchanges, swaps one cryptoasset for another, or operates a machine that does the same thing “by way of business.”</p>
<p>The FCA’s anti-money-laundering regime <a href="https://www.fca.org.uk/firms/financial-crime/money-laundering-terrorist-financing/cryptoassets-aml-ctf-regime">explicitly names</a> “cryptoasset exchange providers,” including p2p providers, as firms that can fall inside the rules. A person who repeatedly buys and sells crypto for others, advertises a service, handles customer money, or acts as a recurring intermediary can’t describe the activity as informal.</p>
<p>Under the UK’s Money Laundering Regulations, in-scope crypto businesses must register with the FCA before they begin operating, and the regulator says registration is a legal requirement.</p>

<div class="cs-article-embed">
    <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/uks-fca-takes-action-against-illegal-crypto-atm-operators/" class="cs-article-embed__link">
                    <div class="cs-article-embed__media">
                <img src="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/bitcoin-atm-london-1024x538.jpg" alt="UK’s FCA takes action against illegal crypto ATM operators" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
            </div>
                <div class="cs-article-embed__body">
            <span class="cs-article-embed__related-reading">Related Reading</span>
            <h3 class="cs-article-embed__title">UK’s FCA takes action against illegal crypto ATM operators</h3>
                            <div class="cs-article-embed__summary">The UK FCA said no crypto ATM operator was registered with it, making their operations illegal in the country.</div>
                                        <div class="cs-article-embed__meta">
                                            <span class="cs-article-embed__meta-item">May 5, 2023</span>
                                                                <span class="cs-article-embed__meta-divider">·</span>
                                                                <span class="cs-article-embed__meta-item">Oluwapelumi Adejumo</span>
                                    </div>
                    </div>
    </a>
</div>

<p>The reason is anti-money laundering. A registered crypto firm has to verify customers, monitor transactions, keep records, and report suspicious activity. These requirements are part of the financial system that makes it harder for stolen funds, sanctions evasion, fraud proceeds, and terrorist financing to move through apparently ordinary payments.</p>
<p>For the FCA, an unregistered peer-to-peer desk creates the same basic risk as any other unregistered money-services business: it can turn dirty money into spendable value while leaving fewer names behind.</p>
<p>There is also the issue of promotions. Since the UK extended its financial promotions regime to crypto, companies marketing crypto activity to UK consumers must use one of four permitted routes.</p>
<p><span style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0px; padding: 0px;">These <a href="https://www.fca.org.uk/firms/cryptoasset-financial-promotions-and-fiat-crypto-ramp-services" target="_blank" rel="noopener">include</a> communication by an authorized firm, approval by an authorized firm, communication by an FCA-registered crypto business under the relevant exemption, or another valid exemption.</span> Promotions outside those routes breach section 21 of the Financial Services and Markets Act and are treated as a criminal offense.</p>
<p>Having tax officials involved in the investigation just makes it more complicated. It doesn’t prove that each target had undeclared income or unpaid tax, but it shows how authorities see informal crypto services.</p>
<p>A business that takes fees, earns spread, or generates gains through repeated dealing can create taxable income. If that business also avoids registration, customer checks, and clean accounting, enforcement turns into financial crime supervision, tax compliance, and consumer protection wrapped into one operation.</p>
<p><a href="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ukcrypto1.png" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-532221 size-full" src="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ukcrypto1.png" alt="The UK draws the line on P2P crypto trading" width="1086" height="1448" srcset="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ukcrypto1.png 1086w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ukcrypto1-225x300.png 225w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ukcrypto1-768x1024.png 768w" sizes="(max-width: 1086px) 100vw, 1086px" /></a></p>
<h2>The UK has already moved crypto inside the perimeter</h2>
<p>The UK has spent years pulling crypto from a semi-detached market into a rule-bound financial box. <em>CryptoSlate</em> has covered that process in several stages, from the FCA’s expanded reach over <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/stablecoin-issuers-and-custodians-in-uk-may-be-regulated-like-banks-next/">stablecoin issuers</a> and custodians to the UK Treasury’s October 2027 deadline for a <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/crypto-investors-gain-critical-protection-in-bankruptcy-even-as-a-conservative-rule-threatens-liquidity/">full cryptoasset regime</a> under FSMA-style rules.</p>

<div class="cs-article-embed">
    <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/stablecoin-issuers-and-custodians-in-uk-may-be-regulated-like-banks-next/" class="cs-article-embed__link">
                    <div class="cs-article-embed__media">
                <img src="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/fca-crypto-regulation-1024x538.jpg" alt="Stablecoin issuers and custodians in UK may be regulated like banks next" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
            </div>
                <div class="cs-article-embed__body">
            <span class="cs-article-embed__related-reading">Related Reading</span>
            <h3 class="cs-article-embed__title">Stablecoin issuers and custodians in UK may be regulated like banks next</h3>
                            <div class="cs-article-embed__summary">FCA warns investors protections are coming but volatility won’t disappear.</div>
                                        <div class="cs-article-embed__meta">
                                            <span class="cs-article-embed__meta-item">Sep 17, 2025</span>
                                                                <span class="cs-article-embed__meta-divider">·</span>
                                                                <span class="cs-article-embed__meta-item">Oluwapelumi Adejumo</span>
                                    </div>
                    </div>
    </a>
</div>

<p>The country has also <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/uk-crypto-property-law-digital-asset-act-2025/">clarified</a> that digital assets can be treated as a third category of personal property, giving courts a firmer basis for ownership, recovery, custody, and insolvency disputes. That legal recognition helps crypto owners when assets are stolen, or platforms fail, and makes crypto easier for regulators, lawyers, and courts to fit into existing enforcement systems.</p>
<p>Recognition and restraint usually arrive together. The more the state accepts crypto as property, market infrastructure, payment technology, or collateral, the more it wants to know who's providing the service, who's responsible when something breaks, and who's checking whether criminal money is moving through the system.</p>
<p>Bitcoin began as a peer-to-peer electronic cash system, and <em>CryptoSlate’s</em> <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/coins/bitcoin/">Bitcoin page</a> still describes it as a decentralized peer-to-peer network secured by cryptographic proof rather than trust in a central authority.</p>
<p>Yet the market surrounding Bitcoin has changed so much that it's almost unrecognizable. A user can still hold private keys, send coins directly, and transact without a bank account, but most large-scale access now runs through exchanges, custodians, ETF issuers, payment firms, and regulated rails.</p>
<p>That creates a legal distinction that regulators can work with. Holding Bitcoin is one thing, but running a recurring business helping strangers buy and sell it is another. Running an informal service that substitutes for an exchange while avoiding the controls that exchanges must follow is exactly the kind of activity the FCA is designed to stop.</p>
<p>Seen that way, the raid is legally clean. The FCA isn’t inventing a new rule on the fly or regulating through enforcement. Its <a href="https://www.fca.org.uk/firms/cryptoassets-aml-ctf-regime/cryptoassets-who-needs-register">guidance</a> states that companies and sole practitioners providing in-scope crypto services in a business capacity must register, and its registration page specifically includes peer-to-peer providers in the category of cryptoasset exchange providers.</p>
<p>The question we have to ask now is what gets lost when the law is enforced this way.</p>
<p><a href="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ukcrypto2.png" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-532220 size-full" src="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ukcrypto2.png" alt="What gets lost as crypto moves inside the UK perimeter?" width="1122" height="1402" srcset="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ukcrypto2.png 1122w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ukcrypto2-240x300.png 240w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ukcrypto2-819x1024.png 819w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ukcrypto2-768x960.png 768w" sizes="(max-width: 1122px) 100vw, 1122px" /></a></p>
<h2>The raid narrows the space where crypto still feels like crypto</h2>
<p>Peer-to-peer crypto has always carried two meanings at once. To regulators, it always looks like a gap in surveillance: direct trades, fewer records, weaker identity checks, and easier movement between cash, bank transfers, stablecoins, and wallets.</p>
<p>But to crypto-native users, it's one of the last visible pieces of the original design: two people exchanging value without asking a bank, broker, app store, payment processor, or exchange for permission.</p>
<p>A person using p2p markets to run an unlicensed exchange isn’t defending financial freedom. They're using the language of decentralization to avoid obligations every other money-handling business has to follow, especially in the UK.</p>
<p>Still, enforcement of this kind changes the shape of the market for people who never planned to commit a crime. When the state squeezes informal exchange, more activity moves onto regulated platforms.</p>
<p>That gives users clearer recourse, better disclosures, and cleaner records. It also means more identity checks, more transaction monitoring, more account freezes, and more dependence on firms that can be pressured, licensed, delisted, acquired, or cut off from banking access.</p>
<p>The first loss is privacy. A regulated exchange creates a record that links a real person to a wallet, a bank account, a device, and a trading history. That record can protect customers in disputes and help police follow stolen money, but it can also turn their crypto use into another monitored financial file.</p>
<p>The second loss is access. People who struggle with banks, lack standard documents, live between jurisdictions, work in cash-heavy industries, or simply distrust large platforms often rely on informal routes into crypto. Some of those routes are messy, some are risky, and some are also the only realistic bridge into a digital asset system that keeps claiming to be open.</p>
<p>The third loss is autonomy. Crypto’s promise was never only price appreciation, although that is what pulled most people in. It was the idea that an individual could hold and transfer value through software, without every transaction being routed through institutional permission.</p>
<p>Each enforcement action that pushes users back toward approved intermediaries makes crypto safer in the way a gated financial system is safer: more controlled, more legible, and more dependent on the gate.</p>
<p>The UK is hardly alone here. <em>CryptoSlate’s</em> <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/every-major-crypto-regulation-change-in-2025-explained-simply/">end-of-the-year review of 2025 regulation</a> described a world in which major jurisdictions began converting crypto from a legal argument to operational infrastructure, with rules on issuers, exchanges, custody, payments, and investor protection becoming more specific. T</p>
<p>he FCA’s London operation fits that global direction. Informal access points are being pulled toward the same perimeter as centralized platforms.</p>
<p>That may help large exchanges and registered firms. It may also make life easier for banks, payment companies, and institutions that want crypto exposure without informal counterparties sitting beside them. The market becomes easier to supervise and easier to plug into traditional finance.</p>
<p>It also becomes less peer-to-peer in the most basic meaning of the phrase.</p>
<p>The uncomfortable middle ground is the honest one. Unregistered crypto dealing can create real risks, and regulation can protect real people.</p>
<p>At the same time, a system that treats every repeat act of informal exchange as a business to be registered, monitored, and supervised leaves less room for the kind of direct financial activity that made crypto culturally powerful in the first place.</p>
<p>The UK may be right on the law. It may even be right on enforcement. The open issue is what kind of crypto market is left once safety, surveillance, access, and autonomy are all forced into the same box.</p>
<p>At some point, making crypto safer also makes it more like the financial system it was built to route around.</p>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>On Apr. 24, Project Eleven awarded its Q-Day Prize to Giancarlo Lelli, a researcher who used publicly accessible quantum hardware to derive a 15-bit elliptic curve private key from its public key.</p>
<p>This is the largest public demonstration to date of the attack class that could one day threaten Bitcoin, Ethereum, and every other system secured by elliptic curve cryptography. The prize was one Bitcoin.</p>
<p>The irony is that a researcher won Bitcoin by breaking a miniature version of the math that protects Bitcoin.</p>
<p>A <strong>15-bit key is nowhere near the security of Bitcoin's 256-bit elliptic curve</strong>, and no publicly known quantum computer can break real Bitcoin wallets today.</p>
<p>The result arrives at a moment when the surrounding context has gotten considerably more serious, with Google cutting its <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/google-slashes-quantum-cracking-estimates-by-20x-creating-600-billion-quantum-countdown-for-bitcoin-and-ethereum/">ECDLP-256 resource estimates</a> and setting a 2029 migration deadline in the same month.</p>
<h2>What Lelli actually did</h2>
<p>Lelli used a variant of Shor's algorithm, a quantum algorithm targeting the elliptic-curve discrete logarithm problem, the mathematical foundation of <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/coins/bitcoin/">Bitcoin's</a> signature scheme, to recover a private key from a public key over a search space of 32,767.</p>
<p>The <a href="https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/project-eleven-awards-1-btc-q-day-prize-for-largest-quantum-attack-on-elliptic-curve-cryptography-to-date-302752439.html">Q-Day Prize competition</a> asked entrants to break the largest possible ECC key on a quantum computer, with no classical shortcuts or hybrid tricks.</p>
<p>Lelli's 15-bit result was the highest any entrant reached by the deadline, and Project Eleven described it as a 512x jump over Steve Tippeconnic's 6-bit September 2025 demonstration.</p>
<p>The winning machine had roughly 70 qubits, per Decrypt's reporting, and an independent panel including researchers from the University of Wisconsin-Madison and qBraid reviewed the submission, according to Project Eleven.</p>
<p>The right frame for this result is a toy lock picked using the same family of methods that would one day threaten the vault. The locksmiths improved, and the vault holds for now.</p>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Claim</th>
<th>What the article supports</th>
<th>Why it matters</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>A quantum computer broke a 15-bit ECC key</td>
<td>Project Eleven says Giancarlo Lelli derived a 15-bit elliptic curve private key from its public key using publicly accessible quantum hardware</td>
<td>It turns the quantum threat into a concrete public demonstration rather than a purely theoretical warning</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Bitcoin itself was not hacked</td>
<td>The article explicitly says no publicly known quantum computer can break real Bitcoin wallets today</td>
<td>This keeps the piece credible and avoids overstating the result</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The result used the same attack family relevant to Bitcoin</td>
<td>Lelli used a variant of Shor’s algorithm targeting the elliptic-curve discrete logarithm problem, which underlies Bitcoin’s signature scheme</td>
<td>It connects the toy demo to the real cryptographic risk without claiming equivalence</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The demo was done under constrained rules</td>
<td>The Q-Day Prize required entrants to break the largest possible ECC key on a quantum computer with no classical shortcuts or hybrid tricks</td>
<td>It strengthens the significance of the result as a quantum benchmark</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The result is larger than prior public ECC demonstrations</td>
<td>Project Eleven described the 15-bit result as a 512x jump over Steve Tippeconnic’s 6-bit September 2025 demonstration</td>
<td>It shows the public demo frontier is advancing</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The gap to Bitcoin’s 256-bit security remains enormous</td>
<td>The article notes that a 15-bit key is nowhere near Bitcoin’s 256-bit elliptic curve security</td>
<td>This is the central caveat readers need in order to interpret the story correctly</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The hardware was still small by real-attack standards</td>
<td>The winning machine reportedly had roughly 70 qubits</td>
<td>It underlines that the achievement is meaningful as a milestone, not as proof that full-scale attacks are imminent</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The real story is directional, not catastrophic</td>
<td>Public demos are getting bigger, resource estimates are falling, and migration deadlines now have concrete dates</td>
<td>The threat is still future tense, but the timeline is getting harder to dismiss</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>The reason this demo lands with more weight than it would have six months ago is Google.</p>
<p>On Mar. 31, <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/companies/google/">Google</a> published new ECDLP-256 resource estimates for circuits using fewer than 1,200 logical qubits and 90 million Toffoli gates, or fewer than 1,450 logical qubits and 70 million Toffoli gates.</p>
<p>Google estimated those circuits could execute on a superconducting cryptographically relevant quantum computer with fewer than 500,000 physical qubits, roughly a 20-fold reduction from prior estimates.</p>
<p>On Mar. 25, Google set a 2029 target for its own post-quantum cryptography migration, tying the deadline explicitly to progress in hardware, error correction, and resource estimates.</p>
<p>Cloudflare <a href="https://blog.cloudflare.com/post-quantum-roadmap/">matched that 2029</a> target on Apr. 7, citing both the Google paper and a Caltech/Oratomic preprint as reasons for acceleration.</p>
<p>That preprint argued that neutral-atom architectures could run Shor's algorithm at cryptographically relevant scales with as few as 10,000 reconfigurable atomic qubits.</p>
<p>Commenting on Apr. 9, QuTech <a href="https://qutech.nl/2026/04/09/expert-commentary-what-do-new-quantum-resource-estimates-mean-for-encryption/">noted that at 10,000 qubits</a>, the architecture would still require nearly three years to break a single ECC-256 key, while the more time-efficient 26,000-qubit configuration would bring the runtime to roughly 10 days.</p>
<p>Both estimates depend on machines that do not yet exist, and the Caltech/Oratomic work is an unreviewed preprint.</p>
<p>The useful takeaway from those numbers is that some theoretical architectures now place the long-term hardware requirement far below what researchers assumed a year ago.</p>
<p>The clocks for public demonstrations are getting shorter, resource estimates are falling, and migration timelines now carry concrete dates.</p>
<figure id="attachment_532102" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-532102" style="width: 1052px" class="wp-caption aligncenter"><img decoding="async" class="wp-image-532102 size-full" src="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/brave_GfovLCJxWv.jpg" alt="Quantum computing recent advancements and how they relate to Bitcoin" width="1052" height="786" srcset="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/brave_GfovLCJxWv.jpg 1052w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/brave_GfovLCJxWv-300x224.jpg 300w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/brave_GfovLCJxWv-1024x765.jpg 1024w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/brave_GfovLCJxWv-768x574.jpg 768w" sizes="(max-width: 1052px) 100vw, 1052px" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-532102" class="wp-caption-text">A timeline graphic charts five milestones from Mar. 25 to Apr. 24, showing how Google, Cloudflare, QuTech, and Project Eleven compressed Bitcoin's quantum risk timeline.</figcaption></figure>
<h2>Bitcoin wallets are already exposed</h2>
<p>Project Eleven's live tracker currently lists 6,934,064 BTC as vulnerable to a quantum attack.</p>
<p>The vulnerability is that quantum attacks are most dangerous when a public key is already visible on-chain, which happens with older address types, reused addresses, and partial spends.</p>
<p>Some Bitcoin wallets have already exposed their public keys through prior transactions. Google's Mar. 31 paper sharpened that picture, noting that fast-clock cryptographically relevant quantum computers could enable on-spend attacks on public mempool transactions, extending the risk from dormant old wallets to live spending.</p>
<p>Bitcoin's governance has begun to respond with BIP 360, which proposes a new output type removing Taproot's quantum-vulnerable key-path spend. BIP 361 <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/bitcoins-quantum-migration-plan-forces-the-community-to-choose-between-frozen-and-stolen-coins/">proposes a phased sunset</a> of legacy signatures that would push quantum-vulnerable outputs toward migration.</p>
<p>Their existence confirms that Bitcoin has entered the migration phase. The harder problem ahead is if a decentralized network can align on incentives, timetables, and the treatment of dormant or lost coins before urgency outruns coordination.</p>
<h2>Two paths forward</h2>
<p>In the bull case, migration becomes routine before any emergency arrives.</p>
<p>Google's and Cloudflare's 2029 targets reset expectations across the industry, wallet providers and <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/exchanges/">exchanges</a> push users away from long-exposure address patterns, and Bitcoin governance coalesces around output changes before any real cryptographically relevant quantum computer materializes.</p>
<p>Q-Day stays future tense, and the most vulnerable stock of BTC tied to exposed public keys shrinks as hardware catches up.</p>
<p>In the bear case, the attack path keeps looking more like engineering than science fiction, outpacing governance's response.</p>
<p>More public key break demonstrations arrive, architecture-specific estimates fall again, and the <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/market/">market</a> starts repricing vulnerable UTXOs and long-idle coins.</p>
<p>The damage in this scenario begins with the erosion of confidence, governance conflict, and rushed migration planning under the clock. A decentralized network with no central authority to mandate deadlines faces the hardest version of that race.</p>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Scenario</th>
<th>What changes</th>
<th>What stays vulnerable</th>
<th>Market / governance implication</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Bull case</td>
<td>Migration becomes routine before any emergency arrives; wallet providers, exchanges, and protocol developers begin reducing public-key exposure</td>
<td>Older address types, reused addresses, and some dormant wallets still carry risk until fully migrated</td>
<td>Confidence holds because the ecosystem treats quantum risk as an infrastructure upgrade rather than a crisis</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Bear case</td>
<td>Public key-break demonstrations keep improving and hardware/resource estimates keep falling faster than governance adapts</td>
<td>Exposed public keys, long-idle coins, partial spends, and live-spend transactions remain exposed for longer</td>
<td>Markets begin repricing vulnerable UTXOs, governance conflict intensifies, and migration happens under pressure</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>What reduces risk fastest</td>
<td>Better wallet hygiene, fewer reused addresses, reduced public-key exposure, adoption of new output types, and phased retirement of legacy signatures</td>
<td>Coordination problems remain, especially around lost coins and slow-moving users</td>
<td>The network buys time and lowers the number of coins exposed before cryptographically relevant quantum machines exist</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>What raises urgency fastest</td>
<td>Larger public demos, lower hardware estimates, faster-clock architectures, and stronger evidence that on-spend or mempool attacks could become practical</td>
<td>Any wallet whose public key is already visible becomes more sensitive to future advances</td>
<td>The debate shifts from “should we prepare?” to “how fast can Bitcoin coordinate?”</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Key external deadlines</td>
<td>Google and Cloudflare target 2029; the UK’s NCSC sets milestones at 2028, 2031, and 2035</td>
<td>Decentralized crypto networks cannot move as quickly as centralized firms by default</td>
<td>Bitcoin faces a harder version of the migration race because it depends on distributed coordination rather than a single authority</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Bottom-line consequence</td>
<td>In the best case, Q-Day stays future tense long enough for migration to get ahead of the threat</td>
<td>In the worst case, technical progress outpaces social and governance response</td>
<td>The real risk is not only eventual key-breaking power, but whether the ecosystem can align before urgency outruns coordination</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>The UK's National Cyber Security Center has <a href="https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/guidance/pqc-migration-timelines">set migration milestones</a> at 2028, 2031, and 2035. Google and Cloudflare both target 2029.</p>
<p>The <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/companies/ethereum-foundation/">Ethereum Foundation</a> says migrating a global decentralized protocol takes years and must begin <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/as-quantum-q-day-jumps-to-2029-ethereum-faces-a-new-fight-over-what-to-do-with-coins-left-in-old-wallets/">before the threat arrives</a>.</p>
<p>Bitcoin's quantum threat now lives in public demonstrations, corporate migration calendars, and draft protocol proposals.</p>
<p>The post <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/latest-quantum-computer-breaks-the-math-behind-bitcoin-headlines-massively-exaggerate-risk/">Latest “quantum computer breaks the math behind Bitcoin” headlines massively exaggerate risk</a> appeared first on <a href="https://cryptoslate.com">CryptoSlate</a>.</p>
]]></content:encoded>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p><a href="https://cryptoslate.com/coins/ethereum/">Ethereum</a> traders are rebuilding bullish exposure to the second-largest cryptocurrency, with derivatives markets showing renewed demand for upside bets.</p>
<p>According to <em>CryptoSlate's</em> data, ETH has gained about 11% this month on the back of a four-week stretch of gains, its longest in nearly a year.</p>
<p>This uptrend pushed ETH to around $2330, its highest price level since February, and puts it on course for its first back-to-back monthly advance since July and August 2025.</p>
<figure id="attachment_532044" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-532044" style="width: 1777px" class="wp-caption aligncenter"><img decoding="async" class="size-full wp-image-532044" src="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Screenshot-2026-04-24-143810.jpg" alt="Ethereum Price " width="1777" height="327" srcset="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Screenshot-2026-04-24-143810.jpg 1777w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Screenshot-2026-04-24-143810-300x55.jpg 300w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Screenshot-2026-04-24-143810-1024x188.jpg 1024w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Screenshot-2026-04-24-143810-768x141.jpg 768w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Screenshot-2026-04-24-143810-1536x283.jpg 1536w" sizes="(max-width: 1777px) 100vw, 1777px" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-532044" class="wp-caption-text">Ethereum Price Monthly Returns Since January 2025 -April 2026 (Source: CoinGlass)</figcaption></figure>
<p>As a result, ETH's price performance has shifted the market attention back to the $3,000 level after months of weaker relative performance against <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/coins/bitcoin/">Bitcoin</a>.</p>
<h2>Ethereum options trader position for $3,200</h2>
<p><a href="https://cryptoslate.com/companies/deribit/">Deribit, the largest crypto options venue</a>, has become the clearest expression of the renewed upside trade.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.deribit.com/statistics/ETH/options-data">Data</a> from the trading platform show that open interest in ETH call options has built up around the $3,200 strike, with more than $322 million in outstanding contracts. The $2,500 strike option follows closely with roughly $320 million in open interest.</p>
<p>Call options give traders the right to buy an asset at a set price. They typically gain value as the underlying token moves closer to the strike.</p>
<p>In ETH's case, the concentration around $2,500 and $3,200 shows that traders are again positioning for a move beyond the current recovery range.</p>
<p>Meanwhile, the <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/insights/ethereum-open-interest-hits-all-time-high-as-price-rises-to-4-month-high/">large open interest</a> does not mean every position is a direct bullish bet. Options activity can include hedging, spread trades, volatility strategies, and market-maker exposure.</p>
<h2>ETH ETF flows register longest inflow streak this year</h2>
<p>US spot <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/xrp-and-solana-dethrone-bitcoin-and-ethereum-as-institutional-favorites-in-2025/">Ethereum exchange-traded funds (ETFs)</a> recently delivered one of the strongest demand signals ahead of the rally, which then paused.</p>
<p>Data from SoSo Value showed that the 10 funds drew more than $633 million during a 10-day inflow streak that began on April 9 and ended on April 22. This is their longest inflow streak of this year and the longest since June 2025.</p>
<figure id="attachment_532043" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-532043" style="width: 1780px" class="wp-caption aligncenter"><img decoding="async" class="size-full wp-image-532043" src="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Screenshot-2026-04-24-143635.jpg" alt="Ethereum ETFs Daily Flows in 2026" width="1780" height="340" srcset="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Screenshot-2026-04-24-143635.jpg 1780w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Screenshot-2026-04-24-143635-300x57.jpg 300w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Screenshot-2026-04-24-143635-1024x196.jpg 1024w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Screenshot-2026-04-24-143635-768x147.jpg 768w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Screenshot-2026-04-24-143635-1536x293.jpg 1536w" sizes="(max-width: 1780px) 100vw, 1780px" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-532043" class="wp-caption-text">Ethereum ETFs Daily Flows in 2026 (Source: SoSoValue)</figcaption></figure>
<p>However, the current inflow streak ended on April 23, when the funds recorded $75.94 million in net outflows, marking their first negative session since early April.</p>
<p>Still, the inflow streak helps support the view that regulated investors were returning to Ethereum exposure after months in which Bitcoin attracted the larger institutional bid. ETF flows are closely watched because they show demand through spot products rather than leveraged positions on derivatives venues.</p>
<p>Alphractal <a href="https://x.com/Alphractal/status/2047344247431668191/photo/1">data</a> corroborated the trend and pointed out that its Ethereum Smart Money Flow Index, a proprietary measure of <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/spot-ethereum-etfs-record-1b-inflows-in-15-trading-days-hitting-4b-for-the-first-time/">institutional activity in ETH,</a> has also shown positive divergence from price for several weeks.</p>
<figure id="attachment_532042" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-532042" style="width: 1000px" class="wp-caption aligncenter"><img decoding="async" class="size-full wp-image-532042" src="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/HGmgvoMaUAAlJfR.jpg" alt="Ethereum Smart Money Flow Index" width="1000" height="562" srcset="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/HGmgvoMaUAAlJfR.jpg 1000w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/HGmgvoMaUAAlJfR-300x169.jpg 300w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/HGmgvoMaUAAlJfR-768x432.jpg 768w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/HGmgvoMaUAAlJfR-480x270.jpg 480w" sizes="(max-width: 1000px) 100vw, 1000px" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-532042" class="wp-caption-text">Ethereum Smart Money Flow Index (Source: Alphractal)</figcaption></figure>
<p>That suggests fund demand had been improving before the recovery became more visible in spot prices.</p>
<p>However, the latest outflow tempers that reading as it shows that Ethereum has not yet shown the same ETF-led consistency that has supported Bitcoin during stronger rallies.</p>
<p>For <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/ethereum-etfs-register-quickest-1b-intake-to-surpass-7b-in-total-inflows/">ETH, the fund-flow</a> picture is improving, but it has not yet become strong enough to carry the market on its own.</p>
<h2>Buyers are gradually returning to the market</h2>
<p>Apart from the sustained inflows from the ETFs, <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/companies/binance/">Binance</a> order-flow data also points to a gradual improvement in demand rather than aggressive accumulation.</p>
<p>CryptoQuant's <a href="https://cryptoquant.com/insights/quicktake/69ea34607c981667c6c2dcbf-Binance-Data-Reveals-a-Gradual-Return-of-Demand-for-Ethereum">data</a> show that the exchange’s Cumulative Volume Delta (CVD) recently registered a positive reading of about 48,400. CVD tracks the net difference between buying and selling volume. A positive reading means buy orders are outweighing sell orders.</p>
<figure id="attachment_532041" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-532041" style="width: 966px" class="wp-caption aligncenter"><img decoding="async" class="size-full wp-image-532041" src="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Screenshot-2026-04-24-143344.jpg" alt="Ethereum Volume Momentum" width="966" height="544" srcset="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Screenshot-2026-04-24-143344.jpg 966w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Screenshot-2026-04-24-143344-300x169.jpg 300w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Screenshot-2026-04-24-143344-768x432.jpg 768w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Screenshot-2026-04-24-143344-480x270.jpg 480w" sizes="(max-width: 966px) 100vw, 966px" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-532041" class="wp-caption-text">Ethereum Volume Momentum (Source: CryptoQuant)</figcaption></figure>
<p>This suggests ETH is not rising solely due to the increased speculative leverage but because buyers have returned to the market, which has helped the token stabilize after earlier declines.</p>
<p>Meanwhile, the relationship between <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/ethereums-hidden-death-spiral-mechanic-could-freeze-800-billion-in-assets-regardless-of-their-safety-rating/">ETH's price</a> and order flow has also strengthened. The correlation coefficient was 0.66, indicating a moderately strong relationship between buying activity and price movement.</p>
<p>However, the signal remains measured because ETH is still trading below prior highs, and the CVD reading does not show the type of forceful spot accumulation usually associated with a confirmed breakout. Instead, it points to a rebalancing phase after a weaker stretch.</p>
<p>That leaves a <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/ethereum-rebound-outperforms-market-amid-strongest-performance-since-2021/">sustained ETH uptrend</a> dependent on whether the improvement in order flow continues.</p>
<p>A stronger CVD reading would support the case that spot buyers are validating the move shown in options and ETFs. A stall would leave the rally more exposed to speculative positioning.</p>
<h2>ETH's leverage is rising</h2>
<p>Despite these bullish metrics, CryptoQuant data from Binance shows the main source of risk behind the ETH rally.</p>
<p>The exchange’s leverage ratio has climbed above the price for the first time in months. When leverage expands faster than spot price gains, it indicates traders are adding borrowed exposure more quickly than investors are buying the token outright.</p>
<figure id="attachment_532040" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-532040" style="width: 1087px" class="wp-caption aligncenter"><img decoding="async" class="size-full wp-image-532040" src="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Screenshot-2026-04-24-143209.jpg" alt="Ethereum Leveraged Ratio" width="1087" height="619" srcset="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Screenshot-2026-04-24-143209.jpg 1087w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Screenshot-2026-04-24-143209-300x171.jpg 300w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Screenshot-2026-04-24-143209-1024x583.jpg 1024w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Screenshot-2026-04-24-143209-768x437.jpg 768w" sizes="(max-width: 1087px) 100vw, 1087px" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-532040" class="wp-caption-text">Ethereum Leveraged Ratio (Source: CryptoQuant)</figcaption></figure>
<p>That pattern can appear during early recoveries, when traders try to position ahead of a breakout before spot flows fully confirm the move.</p>
<p>Notably, this can support fast gains while market conditions remain favorable. It can also increase the risk of forced selling if the price reverses.</p>
<p>However, leveraged positions are more sensitive to moves against them. If ETH fails to hold recent gains, long positions can be liquidated, adding sell pressure to the decline.</p>
<p>This leverage signal sits against a more constructive set of indicators. <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/ethereums-2026-roadmap-just-hit-but-eth-wont-recover-until-one-metric-flips/">Ethereum</a> has posted four straight weekly gains, Deribit traders are targeting higher strikes, ETFs recently recorded a 10-day inflow streak, and CVD shows buy orders outweighing sell orders.</p>
<p>The risk, however, is that those signals are not moving at the same speed.</p>
<p>This is because <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/can-ethereums-strawmap-propel-it-to-10000-by-2029/">ETH's move</a> toward $3,200 would need those gaps to narrow. Spot buyers would need to keep absorbing supply, ETF flows would need to stabilize, and leverage would need to stop rising faster than price.</p>
<p>Without that confirmation, the same derivatives exposure supporting the rebound could amplify losses during a failed breakout.</p>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p><a href="https://cryptoslate.com/coins/bitcoin/">Bitcoin</a> held near $78,000 on Friday as oil prices climbed past $100 a barrel, testing whether the largest digital asset can sustain its April rebound while the US-Iran conflict keeps energy markets on edge.</p>
<p>The move came after President <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/people/donald-trump/">Donald Trump</a> escalated his rhetoric over the <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/crypto-traders-drive-500m-oil-bets-on-hyperliquid-as-hormuz-closure-threatens-100-crude/">Strait of Hormuz</a>, saying the US Navy controlled the waterway and that no ship could enter or leave without American approval.</p>
<p>The comments reinforced fears that the conflict, now centered on maritime leverage rather than direct strikes, could keep one of the world’s most important energy routes shut for longer.</p>
<p>Brent crude <a href="https://oilprice.com/">rose</a> to about $107 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate traded near $97. WTI was on pace for a weekly gain of more than 17% as stalled peace talks, tanker seizures, and the continuing blockade of Hormuz deepened concerns over supply.</p>
<p><a href="https://cryptoslate.com/all-eyes-on-bitcoin-this-weekend-as-iran-is-already-disputing-the-us-version-of-hormuz-deal/">Bitcoin’s response was more measured</a>. The flagship digital asset rose to $78,300 after briefly trading above $79,000 and extended its April recovery by roughly 15%.</p>
<p>The advance came even as US stocks slipped, the dollar strengthened, and traders repriced the risk that higher oil could keep inflation elevated into the Federal Reserve’s next policy meeting.</p>
<p>That combination has turned Bitcoin into a cleaner test of the market’s inflation trade. Traders are weighing whether the token can benefit from renewed demand for scarce assets while avoiding the pressure that a stronger dollar and higher real yields usually place on speculative markets.</p>
<h2>Oil returns to the center of the Bitcoin trade</h2>
<p>The Strait of Hormuz has become the main channel through which <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/bitcoin-jumps-towards-80000-after-strait-of-hormuz-shipping-route-declared-open/">the US-Iran conflict</a> is reaching global markets.</p>
<p>Before the war, about 20 million barrels of oil and petroleum products moved through the waterway each day.</p>
<p>However, shipping has since slowed sharply, with Iran demanding authority over vessel passage and the US blocking Iranian maritime trade. The result is a physical disruption that has carried more weight for traders than the formal ceasefire.</p>
<p>Trump sharpened that pressure Thursday, <a href="https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/116454087460626531">saying</a> on Truth Social that the US had “total control” over the strait and that it would remain “sealed up tight” until Iran reached a deal. He also ordered the Navy to destroy Iranian boats laying mines in the waterway.</p>
<p><a href="https://cryptoslate.com/ceasefire-calmed-hormuz-panic-bitcoin-still-faces-oil-risk/">Oil traders</a> quickly priced the risk of a longer disruption. Brent’s move above $100 revived memories of earlier energy shocks that fed headline inflation and forced central banks to keep policy tighter for longer.</p>
<p>For Bitcoin, that creates a complicated backdrop.</p>
<p>Higher oil supports the argument that investors should own assets outside the fiat system, especially if inflation rises while central banks avoid additional tightening. At the same time, an oil-driven inflation shock can lift the dollar, pressure equity valuations, and reduce liquidity across risk assets.</p>
<p>The first version of that trade helped <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/bitcoin-price-surges-to-78k-even-as-oil-rises-again-creating-new-setup-what-you-need-to-know/">Bitcoin hold its ground</a> on Friday. The second remains the main risk for traders looking for a clean break above $80,000.</p>
<h2>Futures traders drive the move</h2>
<p>The strongest part of Bitcoin’s rally in this market resilience came from derivatives.</p>
<p>CryptoQuant <a href="https://cryptoquant.com/insights/quicktake/69ea28e46aae2d16bb46ebdc-BTCs-Rally-Was-a-Short-Squeeze?utm_source=twitter&utm_medium=sns&utm_campaign=quicktake&utm_content=carmelo-aleman">data</a> showed that Bitcoin’s Thursday surge from $76,351 to $79,447 was driven mainly by futures activity.</p>
<p>According to the firm, open interest climbed from about $24.88 billion to nearly $28 billion as the price moved higher, a pattern that points to leveraged positioning rather than a broad spot-market bid.</p>
<p>The rally forced a large exit from bearish positions. <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/bitcoin-just-wiped-out-600-million-in-bets-triggering-a-mechanical-loop-that-forces-prices-toward-100k/">Bitcoin short liquidations</a> reached about $607.9 million, while Ethereum short liquidations totaled about $581 million. Across the two assets, short liquidations totaled nearly $1.19 billion.</p>
<p>Long liquidations were much smaller. Bitcoin long liquidations totaled about $12.8 million, while Ether long liquidations reached about $98.5 million. Combined long liquidations totaled nearly $111.4 million.</p>
<p>That imbalance explains the speed of the move. Traders who had built short exposure into the March and April weakness were forced to <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/etfs-bleed-818m-bitcoin-slides-81k-1-7b-liquidated/">buy back positions as Bitcoin broke higher</a>. The buying added fuel to the rally, pushing the price quickly toward $79,000.</p>
<p>Alphractal data had flagged the same pressure before the move. Bitcoin perpetual futures funding had stayed negative on a 30-day average basis for 46 straight days, while open interest rose about 12% over that period.</p>
<figure id="attachment_531977" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-531977" style="width: 1000px" class="wp-caption aligncenter"><img decoding="async" class="size-full wp-image-531977" src="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/HGlrAqzbQAAzAFH.jpg" alt="Bitcoin Key Market Metrics" width="1000" height="566" srcset="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/HGlrAqzbQAAzAFH.jpg 1000w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/HGlrAqzbQAAzAFH-300x170.jpg 300w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/HGlrAqzbQAAzAFH-768x435.jpg 768w" sizes="(max-width: 1000px) 100vw, 1000px" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-531977" class="wp-caption-text">Bitcoin Key Market Metrics (Source: Alphractal)</figcaption></figure>
<p>This negative funding means bearish traders were paying to keep positions open, a crowded setup that can unravel quickly when the price turns.</p>
<p>The squeeze gave <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/how-150-billion-was-liquidated-from-crypto-market-in-2025-driving-bitcoin-crash/">Bitcoin momentum</a>, though it also raised the bar for follow-through. A derivatives-led rally can extend if spot buyers step in after the breakout. Without that confirmation, the move can fade once forced buying slows.</p>
<h2>Options market stays cautious</h2>
<p>Meanwhile, <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/bitcoin-braces-for-8b-options-expiry-as-war-oil-and-the-fed-threaten-a-volatility-reset/">options traders are giving Bitcoin</a> room to rise without showing the kind of aggressive upside chasing that often marks overheated conditions.</p>
<p>Greeks.live <a href="https://x.com/GreeksLive/status/2047349175621431326">data</a> showed that 109,000 Bitcoin options expired Friday with a put-call ratio of 0.93, a max pain level of $72,000, and a notional value of $8.55 billion.</p>
<figure id="attachment_531976" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-531976" style="width: 2047px" class="wp-caption aligncenter"><img decoding="async" class="size-full wp-image-531976" src="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/HGmkxS8aUAAd1Zo.jpg" alt="Bitcoin Options Market Expiry for April" width="2047" height="640" srcset="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/HGmkxS8aUAAd1Zo.jpg 2047w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/HGmkxS8aUAAd1Zo-300x94.jpg 300w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/HGmkxS8aUAAd1Zo-1024x320.jpg 1024w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/HGmkxS8aUAAd1Zo-768x240.jpg 768w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/HGmkxS8aUAAd1Zo-1536x480.jpg 1536w" sizes="(max-width: 2047px) 100vw, 2047px" /><figcaption id="caption-attachment-531976" class="wp-caption-text">Bitcoin Options Market Expiry for April (Source: Greeks.live)</figcaption></figure>
<p>The firm said 25% of open options were set to expire in the monthly settlement, with 12% of open interest maturing at the end of May and 24% at the end of June.</p>
<p>Bitcoin’s implied volatility has continued to fall across major maturities, with several tenors slipping by 1 to 2 percentage points and moving below 40%. Skew metrics have also pulled back, signaling that the rebound has not been dominated by panic buying of upside exposure.</p>
<p>That leaves Bitcoin in a steadier position than the size of <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/bitcoin-21-days-true-bull-market-rally-shorts-pile-in-just-spot-demand-pushing-back/">the short squeeze</a> might suggest. Traders are not ignoring the rally, but they are not aggressively paying for calls.</p>
<p>Essentially, the options market is leaving space for a continuation while still pricing the risk that oil, the dollar and Fed expectations can interrupt the move.</p>
<p>However, Andre Dragosch, Bitwise Europe’s head of research, <a href="https://x.com/Andre_Dragosch/status/2047214530975957441">noted</a> that several macro forces still favor Bitcoin. He pointed to fading recession risks, declining real interest rates if the Fed stays on hold while inflation rises, and a large gap between Bitcoin and global money supply trends.</p>
<p>In that framework, financial repression remains one of the strongest environments for the asset.</p>
<p>That view has gained traction as oil’s rally places the Fed in a narrower lane. If policymakers cut rates while energy prices remain elevated, real yields could fall, strengthening Bitcoin’s appeal.</p>
<p>On the other hand, if policymakers stay restrictive to contain inflation expectations, Bitcoin’s April rebound could face the same pressure that weighed on the asset earlier this year.</p>
<p>For now, traders are treating $78,000 as the first line of evidence. Holding that level through an oil spike, a firmer dollar, and weaker equities suggests demand has improved. However, a failed push through $80,000 would leave the move vulnerable to the same macro forces that drove previous pullbacks.</p>

]]></content:encoded>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>I believe the hardest question for DeFi in 2026 is whether the original dream is still alive.</p>
<p>The collective bargain was simple. Users would <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/the-keys-to-sovereignty-why-this-time-is-different/">hold their own keys</a>. Code would execute the rules. Markets would stay open. Ledgers would be visible.</p>
<p>Intermediaries would lose power because financial services could run on public smart contracts rather than private balance sheets.</p>
<p>That framing explains why decentralized finance grew so quickly after 2020. It also explains why the current moment feels so deflating.</p>
<p>I'd like to preface this piece by saying that I believe decentralized finance is an essential part of the world I want to live in. However, I'm also not a zealot for a system that has failed to deliver on its promises.</p>
<p>I believe in “strong opinions, loosely held,” and my conviction on DeFi is pretty loose right now.</p>

<div class="cs-article-embed">
    <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/six-years-after-defi-summer-is-the-sun-already-setting-on-the-decentralized-finance-revolution/" class="cs-article-embed__link">
                    <div class="cs-article-embed__media">
                <img src="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/defi-hack-trust-war-1024x576.webp" alt="Six years after “DeFi Summer” is the sun already setting on the decentralized finance revolution?" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
            </div>
                <div class="cs-article-embed__body">
            <span class="cs-article-embed__related-reading">Related Reading</span>
            <h3 class="cs-article-embed__title">Six years after “DeFi Summer” is the sun already setting on the decentralized finance revolution?</h3>
                            <div class="cs-article-embed__summary">DeFi hits "trust squeeze" as hacks erode credibility and TradFi's tokenization surge could push it into something darker</div>
                                        <div class="cs-article-embed__meta">
                                            <span class="cs-article-embed__meta-item">Apr 20, 2026</span>
                                                                <span class="cs-article-embed__meta-divider">·</span>
                                                                <span class="cs-article-embed__meta-item">Liam 'Akiba' Wright</span>
                                    </div>
                    </div>
    </a>
</div>

<p>The sector has now lived through years of bridge exploits, price manipulation, smart contract failures, wallet compromises, governance fights, and public liquidity stress. At the same time, institutions are adopting tokenization, digital cash, and settlement rails while leaving much of the permissionless political project behind.</p>
<p>The most defensible take is now much narrower than the old promise. DeFi proved that public settlement, automated markets, composability, and transparent ledgers can operate at meaningful scale.</p>
<p>It has yet to prove that those properties, by themselves, create a safer, more decentralized, or more accessible finance than the system it set out to challenge.</p>

<div class="cs-article-embed">
    <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/the-keys-to-sovereignty-why-this-time-is-different/" class="cs-article-embed__link">
                    <div class="cs-article-embed__media">
                <img src="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/bitcoin-sovereign-1024x538.jpg" alt="The keys to sovereignty: Why this time is different" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
            </div>
                <div class="cs-article-embed__body">
            <span class="cs-article-embed__related-reading">Related Reading</span>
            <h3 class="cs-article-embed__title">The keys to sovereignty: Why this time is different</h3>
                            <div class="cs-article-embed__summary">New infrastructure empowers Bitcoin holders to earn yields while maintaining control over their digital assets.</div>
                                        <div class="cs-article-embed__meta">
                                            <span class="cs-article-embed__meta-item">Feb 9, 2025</span>
                                                                <span class="cs-article-embed__meta-divider">·</span>
                                                                <span class="cs-article-embed__meta-item">Laura Wallendal</span>
                                    </div>
                    </div>
    </a>
</div>

<h2>The original bargain had a hidden dependency stack</h2>
<p>The institutional case for DeFi describes its core appeal: <a href="https://institutions.ethereum.org/defi">open financial systems</a> built on smart contracts and shared public infrastructure. That was the optimistic version of the pitch.</p>
<p>Anyone with a wallet could access markets, move collateral, borrow, lend, trade, and inspect the rules. The system would be transparent by default, with settlement happening on-chain rather than inside private institutional ledgers.</p>
<p>The complication is that decentralization was always a layered concept. Vitalik Buterin's older framework separated decentralization into <a href="https://medium.com/@VitalikButerin/the-meaning-of-decentralization-a0c92b76a274">architectural, political, and logical dimensions</a>.</p>
<p>A system can be architecturally decentralized because it runs across many machines, while remaining politically concentrated if decisions rest with a small group of tokenholders, teams, multisigs, foundations, front-end operators, or infrastructure providers.</p>
<p>That split is essential because much of DeFi looked decentralized at the transaction layer while remaining dependent on concentrated forms of control elsewhere.</p>
<p>The Bank for International Settlements made a sharp institutional critique in 2021 that many of us likely scoffed at at the time. It called DeFi's decentralization a <a href="https://www.bis.org/publ/qtrpdf/r_qt2112b.htm">structural illusion</a> because governance needs make some centralization inevitable, and because token and validator economics can concentrate power.</p>
<p>BIS was drawing a line between automated settlement and unavoidable decision-making. Protocols still needed decisions about upgrades, risk parameters, collateral listings, incentives, oracle choices, emergency controls, and treasury use.</p>
<p>Those decisions rarely emerged from a perfectly dispersed public. They usually passed through identifiable governance channels and actors. The <a href="https://www.bis.org/publ/bppdf/bispap122.htm">paper version</a> carries the same institutional critique for policy readers.</p>
<p>The Financial Stability Board added another constraint in 2023. DeFi, it said, had remained mainly <a href="https://www.fsb.org/2023/02/the-financial-stability-risks-of-decentralised-finance/">self-referential</a>, with products and services interacting with other DeFi products rather than the real economy.</p>
<p>It also inherited familiar vulnerabilities from traditional finance, including leverage, liquidity mismatch, operational fragility, and interconnectedness. The process was new. The risk family was older.</p>
<p>A later governance paper from the ECB reinforced the same direction of travel by focusing on <a href="https://www.ecb.europa.eu/pub/pdf/scpwps/ecb.wp3208~051a880042.en.pdf">identifiable actors within DeFi governance</a>.</p>
<p>That lands us at this. DeFi reduced reliance on banks for certain transactions, but it increased reliance on code, bridges, governance, front ends, wallets, oracles, custodial touchpoints, and security teams.</p>
<p>It shifted trust rather than removing it. That shift created genuine transparency. It also created new failure modes.</p>
<p><a href="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ChatGPT-Image-Apr-23-2026-04_09_57-PM.png" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-531908 size-full" src="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ChatGPT-Image-Apr-23-2026-04_09_57-PM.png" alt="DeFi's original bargain ran into a hidden control layer" width="1024" height="1536" srcset="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ChatGPT-Image-Apr-23-2026-04_09_57-PM.png 1024w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ChatGPT-Image-Apr-23-2026-04_09_57-PM-200x300.png 200w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ChatGPT-Image-Apr-23-2026-04_09_57-PM-683x1024.png 683w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ChatGPT-Image-Apr-23-2026-04_09_57-PM-768x1152.png 768w" sizes="(max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px" /></a></p>
<h2>The security record broke the cleanest version of the pitch</h2>
<p>The strongest evidence against DeFi's original security pitch is the record of thefts in 2021 and 2022. A Chainalysis review put DeFi hack losses at <a href="https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/crypto-hacking-stolen-funds-2024/">about $2.5 billion in 2021, $3.1 billion in 2022, and $1.1 billion in 2023</a>.</p>
<p>Since 2023, almost $7 billion has been stolen as hacks continue, and now AI models are creating a new (perhaps even scarier) attack vector.</p>
<p>The 2022 figure was especially damaging. Hackers stole $3.8 billion from crypto businesses overall that year alone, and DeFi protocols accounted for 82.1% of the funds stolen.</p>
<p>Cross-chain bridges made up 64% of the DeFi total, according to <a href="https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/2022-biggest-year-ever-for-crypto-hacking/">a 2022 hacking analysis</a>.</p>
<p>Those numbers changed the meaning of transparency. DeFi users could see what happened. They could follow stolen funds, inspect transactions, and watch governance respond.</p>
<p>Public ledgers made the failures immediate and brutally legible. A bank breach can take months to identify and disclose. A drained pool becomes visible in the block where it happens.</p>

<p>The recent rise in crypto theft has a different composition from the 2021-2022 DeFi exploit cycle. The <a href="https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/crypto-hacking-stolen-funds-2025/">2024 hacking review</a> showed losses rising again as attacker focus shifted toward private-key and centralized-service targets.</p>
<p>The <a href="https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/2025-crypto-crime-report-introduction/">2025 crime trend summary</a> highlighted private-key compromises as a major vector. The <a href="https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/2025-crypto-crime-mid-year-update/">mid-year 2025 update</a> showed the escalation after Bybit before the year-end picture was complete.</p>
<p>The <a href="https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/crypto-hacking-stolen-funds-2026/">2026 report preview</a> then described more than $3.4 billion stolen in 2025, with the Bybit compromise alone accounting for about $1.5 billion.</p>
<p>TRM's <a href="https://www.trmlabs.com/reports-and-whitepapers/2025-crypto-crime-report">2025 Crypto Crime Report</a> provides the prior-year baseline, while its <a href="https://www.trmlabs.com/reports-and-whitepapers/2026-crypto-crime-report">2026 Crypto Crime Report</a> puts 2025 hack losses at $2.87 billion, with Bybit at $1.46 billion, or 51% of that total.</p>
<p>That nuance helps DeFi on one axis and hurts it on another. DeFi protocol exploit losses appeared to have improved since the 2022 peak.</p>
<p>At the same time, the broader crypto stack still looks brittle, seems to be surging again through new AI tooling, and DeFi's original user-sovereignty pitch depends on that broader stack.</p>
<p>If the wallet, signing process, bridge, front end, governance channel, or collateral wrapper becomes the weak point, the user experiences a system failure. Dynamic incident databases<span style="box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0px; padding: 0px;">, such as <a href="https://defillama.com/hacks" target="_blank" rel="noopener">DeFiLlama's hacks tracker,</a> exist because the failure surface remains wide and constantly evolving</span>.</p>
<p>Thinking back, one of the DeFi projects I was excited about in 2021 was PancakeBunny. It was a small project, but I liked the UI, the branding, the infrastructure, and I even bought some merch. I was wearing the hoodie this week when I took a moment to think back to all the other DeFi projects that had similar or greater potential and have simply died. It almost seems that the official product life cycle in DeFi includes a hack, an exploit, a pump-and-dump, or insolvency.</p>
<blockquote><p>“On a long enough timeline, the survival rate for all [DeFi projects] drops to zero.” – Chuck Palahniuk, Fight Club</p></blockquote>
<p>While a fairly niche project, I think PancakeBunny is a useful example because it condensed the emotional cycle into a single event. Rekt reported that a May 2021 <a href="https://rekt.news/pancakebunny-rekt/">flash-loan manipulation</a> hit the protocol for about $45 million, pushed BUNNY from $146 to $6, and struck after the protocol had once held more than $10 billion in TVL.</p>
<p>The case looks like an early template: unknown protocol, rapid yield-driven growth, giant TVL, manipulation, collapse, then a token chart that never recovers the old story.</p>
<p>That pattern is why the security question carries more weight than any single hack. DeFi promised an alternative trust model. For many users, it became a new risk stack with fewer intermediaries to complain to when something broke.</p>
<h2>Aave shows how mature DeFi stress now unfolds in public</h2>
<p><a href="/aave/">Aave</a> is a better current test than most smaller protocols because it remains one of DeFi's core lending venues. If a marginal farm fails, the conclusion says little about the system.</p>
<p>If a leading lending protocol is forced into visible crisis management, the implication is wider.</p>
<p>The April 2026 rsETH incident is therefore important, but it needs careful language. The Aave incident report said the event originated outside Aave, from Kelp's LayerZero V2 Unichain to Ethereum rsETH route, which had been configured as a 1-of-1 DVN path.</p>
<p>The report said a forged inbound packet released 116,500 rsETH from the Ethereum-side adapter, and that 89,567 rsETH were deposited on Aave. It also stated that Aave's smart contracts were not compromised and that Aave's protocol logic continued to function as designed.</p>
<p>The <a href="https://governance.aave.com/t/rseth-incident-report-april-20-2026/24580">Aave governance report</a> framed the issue as collateral, bridge, and external-asset risk rather than an exploit of Aave itself.</p>
<p>That caveat protects Aave from a false claim that its own contracts were hacked. It also reinforces the deeper DeFi problem.</p>
<p>In a composable system, a protocol can behave correctly and still inherit stress from the asset, bridge, oracle, market, or governance decision it accepted into its risk perimeter.</p>
<p>The report modeled hypothetical bad-debt scenarios ranging from about $123.7 million to $230.1 million, depending on how losses were allocated.</p>
<p>It also described defensive actions, including freezes of rsETH and wrsETH reserves across Aave V3 deployments, WETH freezes on several markets, and interest-rate adjustments.</p>
<p>That is a mature response system. It is also an admission that mature DeFi requires circuit breakers, guardians, risk stewards, emergency parameter changes, and coordinated governance.</p>
<p>The public forum made the human side visible. One Aave governance post argued that ETH price appreciation could worsen the bad-debt gap over time because some liabilities were effectively fixed in ETH terms while available backstops were denominated in stablecoins and dollars.</p>
<p>Other replies disputed parts of the framing, narrowed the issue to L2 exposure, or urged emergency coordination. The <a href="https://governance.aave.com/t/eth-price-appreciation-makes-this-bad-debt-crisis-worse-every-hour-governance-must-move-fast/24495">forum discussion</a> should be treated as live stakeholder pressure with unresolved accounting.</p>
<p><em>CryptoSlate</em> has tracked adjacent Aave pressure, including <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/aave-contributor-exits-put-25b-lending-lead-to-the-test/">contributor departures testing Aave's lending lead</a> and <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/aave-prices-are-crashing-as-insiders-warn-a-hostile-holiday-vote-could-destroy-the-protocols-dominance/">governance conflict around protocol dominance</a>.</p>
<p>Still, the public nature of the debate is the point. DeFi crises happen in view. Depositors, borrowers, tokenholders, analysts, and competitors can watch the governance process unfold.</p>
<p>That gives DeFi a transparency advantage over closed financial systems. It also exposes how much judgment remains inside a supposedly automated system.</p>
<p><a href="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ChatGPT-Image-Apr-23-2026-04_07_53-PM.png" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-531907 size-full" src="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ChatGPT-Image-Apr-23-2026-04_07_53-PM.png" alt="Aave shows how DeFi stress is managed in public" width="1536" height="1024" srcset="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ChatGPT-Image-Apr-23-2026-04_07_53-PM.png 1536w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ChatGPT-Image-Apr-23-2026-04_07_53-PM-300x200.png 300w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ChatGPT-Image-Apr-23-2026-04_07_53-PM-1024x683.png 1024w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ChatGPT-Image-Apr-23-2026-04_07_53-PM-768x512.png 768w" sizes="(max-width: 1536px) 100vw, 1536px" /></a></p>
<h2>The TradFi comparison is real, but the math is uneven</h2>
<p>The claim that DeFi looks less secure than traditional finance needs more care and consideration of nuance than sentiment allows these days.</p>
<p>Traditional finance suffers serious cyber incidents, fraud, operational failures, and data breaches. The difference is that those failures move through legal, regulatory, insurance, and disclosure systems that are much slower and less visible than blockchains.</p>
<p>A bank's customer database breach, an outage, a business-email compromise, and a direct theft from a crypto bridge are all security events. They sit in different categories.</p>
<p>The U.S. public-company disclosure regime illustrates the difference. The SEC requires domestic public companies to disclose material cybersecurity incidents on Form 8-K within <a href="https://www.sec.gov/corpfin/secg-cybersecurity">four business days after determining materiality</a>.</p>
<p>The deadline starts from the materiality determination rather than the first suspicious log entry. That gives companies time to assess scope, legal exposure, operational impact, and national-security considerations.</p>
<p>Bank regulators use another channel. The OCC's computer-security incident notification rule requires a bank to notify its primary federal regulator as soon as possible and no later than <a href="https://www.occ.treas.gov/news-issuances/bulletins/2021/bulletin-2021-55.html">36 hours after determining</a> that a notification incident occurred.</p>
<p>That is a regulatory notification channel rather than a public blockchain ledger.</p>
<p>Cost data shows the scale while preserving the comparison limit. IBM reported that financial industry enterprises averaged <a href="https://www.ibm.com/think/insights/cost-of-a-data-breach-2024-financial-industry?rel=nofollow">$6.08 million per data breach in 2024</a>, above the global average, and that breaches involving 50 million or more records averaged $375 million.</p>
<p>It also put the average identification time for financial firms at 168 days and containment at 51 days. Those figures show that TradFi security failures can be expensive and slow to surface.</p>
<p>Of the 600 breaches analyzed in IBM’s 2025 <a href="https://www.ibm.com/downloads/documents/us-en/131cf87b20b31c91">report</a>, an implied aggregate cost of about $2.66 billion, based on the reported global average breach cost of $4.44 million</p>
<p>So perhaps, DeFi is not dying because it's less secure than TradFi, but its transparency and immediate public impact create an unsolvable marketing problem.</p>
<p>The amount lost to exploits across DeFi and TradFi appears comparable using the figures above. Around $2.6 billion was lost in TradFi in 2025 and $2.8 billion in DeFi.</p>
<p>However, DeFi moved roughly $10 to $13 trillion last year, while over $28 trillion passed through Mastercard and Visa payment rails alone. When you add in FX markets and Fed funds, you move into the quadrillions in TradFi volume.</p>
<p>Using some napkin math, we can estimate DeFi's total volume ceiling at around $46 trillion and TradFi's at around $3.5 quadrillion. Therefore, losses work out to roughly 0.006% of volume in DeFi, compared to 0.00007% in TradFi. This is an 86-fold higher loss rate in DeFi, or 8,500%.</p>
<p>So that's part marketing and PR issue, but mostly a reliability red flag.</p>
<p>IC3 data adds another layer. The FBI said its 2025 Internet Crime Report showed <a href="https://www.fbi.gov/news/press-releases/cryptocurrency-and-ai-scams-bilk-americans-of-billions">nearly $21 billion in cyber-enabled crime losses</a> reported by Americans, with more than $11 billion tied to cryptocurrency complaints.</p>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>The March and April 2026 drawdown has structural consequences, as Bitcoin ETF holders stayed steady.</p>
<p>Bitcoin sits near $78,000, roughly 38% below the $125,761 peak from Oct. 6, and US spot Bitcoin ETFs pulled in $1.32 billion in March, reversing a four-month outflow streak. Then, the ETFs added another $2.42 billion in net inflows between Apr. 6 and Apr. 22.</p>
<p>The strongest days were Apr. 17, with <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/bitcoin-etfs-pull-in-664-million-after-strait-of-hormuz-reopened/">$663.9 million in inflows</a>, and Apr. 22, with $335.8 million in inflows. <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/companies/gemini/">Gemini's</a> coin-level data show that ETF-held Bitcoin fell only from 1.38 million BTC at the October 2025 high to 1.28 million at the trough, then recovered quickly to 1.31 million.</p>

<p>During an interview with Crypto Prime, Bloomberg senior ETF analyst <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/people/eric-balchunas/">Eric Balchunas</a> said that during a 20% drawdown, ETFs logged <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h8XjIl2zSRw">outflows of under $1 billion</a>, roughly 99.5% of their assets. This happened during a genuinely hostile macro window.</p>
<p><a href="https://cryptoslate.com/companies/nasdaq/">Nasdaq's</a> March update showed a 21% decline in the total digital asset <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/market/">market</a> cap across the first quarter, while the Nasdaq-100 fell 4.9% and the S&P 500 fell 5.1%. ETF holders absorbed all of that without producing the exit wave skeptics had forecast.</p>
<p>Balchunas argued that the selling pressure came from longer-tenured crypto holders, saying that the call was “coming from inside the house.”</p>
<p>The <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/etf/">ETF</a> analyst's interpretation fits the flow data, as net ETF buying held through a historically steep drawdown while something else pushed <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/price-watch/">the price</a> lower.</p>

<h2>A different kind of buyer</h2>
<p>The ETF wrapper places <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/coins/bitcoin/">Bitcoin</a> inside model portfolios, advisor guardrails, committee-approved position limits, and rebalancing schedules.</p>
<p>Buyers inside those structures operate during regular <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/trading/">trading</a> hours, so the rules constrain them. In a drawdown, constraint looks like discipline.</p>
